summary: Reviewed mcp-server/gui/api.ts and test files. WP-004 correctly adds backslash guards to assertSafeWpId() and assertSafeQueueId(), but assertSafeSlug() (guarding 14+ handlers with path.join(ledgerRoot, slug, ...)) was not updated. This inconsistency is a Medium A01 (Broken Access Control) finding on Windows — not blocking. 0 Critical, 0 High, 1 Medium (noted). Security sign-off: PASS.

comments.note: A01 (Broken Access Control) — Medium: assertSafeSlug() in mcp-server/gui/api.ts (line 97) was NOT updated by WP-004 to include the backslash check. It guards 14+ call sites (lines 505, 586, 615, 652, 694, 739, 784, 818, 844, 927, 1022, 1089, 1167, 1299, 1353, 1428, etc.) that all pass the slug directly to path.join(ledgerRoot, slug, ...). On Windows, a slug containing backslash path components (e.g. 'project\\..\\..\\secret') would be treated as a directory separator by Node.js path.join(), enabling escape from ledgerRoot. While CORS restricts browser-based access to http://localhost:{port}, the server binds to all interfaces (server.listen(port) with no hostname — line 833 of server.ts), so non-browser HTTP clients on the LAN are not constrained by CORS. WP-004 correctly updated 2 of 3 guard functions but missed assertSafeSlug(). Remediation: add id.includes('\\\\') to assertSafeSlug() alongside the existing '/' and '..' checks — consistent with the pattern applied to assertSafeWpId() and assertSafeQueueId() in this WP. Not blocking: medium severity does not prevent PASS, but should be addressed in a follow-up WP.

Defence-in-depth: all three guard functions (assertSafeSlug, assertSafeWpId, assertSafeQueueId) use a blocklist approach. As noted by Developer and QA, a strict allowlist regex (e.g. /^[\\w.-]+$/) would be more robust — it blocks any unexpected character class by default rather than requiring individual blocklist additions. Recommended for a future hardening pass.

Recommended for a hardening pass that consolidates all three functions.
